referenced_message.content:
Yeah I do think it comes down to a difference in vision for the most part.

I don't think one or two super teams existing would have an impact on players to the point of making them unmotivated to play at all without monetary incentive. I think if anything this is way more reliant on there being clearly worst performing teams, and while I can see how market helps balance out players more to stop this from happening, I don't think it works well enough to completely stop it to a point that's meaningful. For the record I'd also want the league to go down to less teams, which would imo help way more with having a lack of player talent on some teams than market does.

I also don't think that being able to freely form teams would just make the game turn into the same friend groups fighting every season. Even with the plans that were made for teams before the season started there weren't really a lot of pure friendship teams, or teams that looked the same as last season. People will imo naturally want to move to other teams and team with other players, and if anything this would just look closer to teams in other sports having franchise players or core parts of their team, while other players rotate around them. 

I think the only team that's a bad ish offender about this is femme, but that's more so because of our nature as diversity team / having people that would be uncomfortable with players on a lot of other teams. That also ties into more of my issues with market, as I think a big issue is how people can potentially end up on teams they aren't comfortable on, which imo is one reason behind players who do the whole "if you pick me I retire" thing, that's largely ignored right now, for how big of a factor it is for some people. I do agree that people who say they will only play for 1 team for reasons like wanting an op team aren't cool tho, although I think there is a lot to talk about in how much the IBL should be accessible for people with very narrow team wishes / wanting to play with friends primarily
